class.name: MeshInstance4D
class.brief_description: Instance of a 4D mesh in the scene.
class.description: MeshInstance4D is a node that places a [Mesh4D] in the 4D scene. Meshes are used to visibly represent objects in 4D, just like how [MeshInstance3D] is used in 3D scenes. The geometry of the mesh is defined by the [Mesh4D] assigned to the [member mesh] property. This may be set to any [Mesh4D] derived class. [TetraMesh4D] allows for tetrahedral meshes, which are the equivalent of triangles in 3D. [WireMesh4D] allows for wireframe meshes, which behave very similarly to wireframes in 3D. Meshes may have their appearance modified by setting a [Material4D]. There are [TetraMaterial4D] and [WireMaterial4D] classes that are meant to be used with [TetraMesh4D] and [WireMesh4D] derived classes, respectively. Materials may be set on the [Mesh4D] itself, or overridden on a per-instance basis by setting the [member material_override] property on MeshInstance4D.

method.name: get_active_material
method.description: Returns the currently active [Material4D] for the surface of [member mesh] at [param surface_index]. The index only matters for a [MultiSurfaceMesh4D], since a [SingleSurfaceMesh4D] only has surface [code]0[/code]. This is the material that rendering engines use to draw that surface. If [member material_overrides] has a single element, it is returned for every surface. Otherwise, the element at [param surface_index] is returned if there is one and it is not null. Otherwise, the surface's own [member SingleSurfaceMesh4D.material] is returned if it is set. Otherwise, the surface's fallback material is returned (see [method SingleSurfaceMesh4D._get_fallback_material]), which may be null if the surface has no fallback material. Materials found through the overrides or the surface are validated against the surface before being returned, but fallback materials are not. If [member mesh] is not set, or [param surface_index] does not refer to a surface of the mesh, only the overrides are consulted, so this returns the override for that index or null.

members.member: The [Material4D] override used to render the mesh. This material defines the appearance of the mesh, including its color, texture, and lighting properties. The [TetraMaterial4D] type is intended for tetrahedral meshes, and the [WireMaterial4D] type is intended for wireframe meshes. This property overrides the per-mesh material set on the [Mesh4D] resource in the [member SingleSurfaceMesh4D.material] property.

The [Material4D] overrides used to render the multiple surfaces of the mesh. If this array has a single element, it applies to all surfaces. If it has multiple elements, each element corresponds to a specific surface of the mesh. See also [member material_override].

The [Mesh4D] resource that defines the geometry of the mesh. This may be set to any [Mesh4D] derived class. [TetraMesh4D] allows for tetrahedral meshes, which are the equivalent of triangles in 3D. [WireMesh4D] allows for wireframe meshes, which behave very similarly to wireframes in 3D.
